facts: Q4 2025 revenue came at the high end of guidance at $7.3 million, down from $10.1 million in Q3, and the company believes Q4 represented the revenue bottom.
High-power markets represented the majority of total revenue for the first time in Q4, while Mobile declined to less than 25% of revenue and is expected to become insignificant by end of 2026.
Q1 2026 revenue is guided to $8 million to $8.5 million with gross margin of 38.7% plus or minus 25 basis points, representing the first quarter-over-quarter growth since the company's pivot.
The company completed a private placement of common stock in November 2025 with net proceeds of approximately $96 million, contributing to a quarter-end cash balance of $237 million with no debt.
Full year 2025 revenue was $45.9 million compared to $83.3 million in 2024, with full year gross margin of 38.4% versus 40.4% last year.

The company executed a 19% workforce reduction in Q4 and consolidated distribution channel partners from approximately 40 to fewer than 10, with operating expenses targeted to remain flat at approximately $15 million per quarter throughout 2026.

Q4 GAAP results included a $16.6 million restructuring and impairment charge consisting of approximately $10 million in distribution contract terminations, $4 million in fixed asset impairments, and $2 million in workforce reduction expenses.
The company's serviceable addressable market is projected at $3.5 billion by 2030, split roughly 50-50 between GaN and high-voltage SiC, with a combined CAGR of more than 60%.

The company announced a long-term strategic technology and manufacturing partnership with GlobalFoundries to accelerate GaN design and manufacturing in the U.S., with production expected to begin later in the year and accelerate in 2027.
CFO Todd Glickman announced his departure after 10 years of service, with a successor expected to be communicated in the coming weeks.
Q3 FY2026 revenue declined 5% to $1.3 billion, slightly better than the company's prior outlook.

Q3 gross margin declined 310 basis points year-over-year to 44.4%, with 200 basis points of pressure from higher U.S. tariffs and 140 basis points from pricing headwinds in a more promotional North America environment.

A $99 million litigation reserve expense related to an insurance carrier dispute and a $247 million non-cash valuation allowance against U.S. federal deferred tax assets drove a reported diluted loss per share of $1.01, while adjusted diluted EPS was $0.09.

The company raised its full year adjusted operating income outlook to approximately $110 million, at the high end of the prior $95 million to $110 million range, and now expects adjusted diluted EPS of $0.10 to $0.11.

Full year FY2026 revenue is now expected to decline approximately 4% (versus prior guidance of 4% to 5%), with North America down approximately 8%, APAC down approximately 6%, and EMEA growing approximately 9%.

Year-to-date footwear sales are down about 14%, and Q3 footwear revenue decreased 12%, reflecting structural issues the company is actively unwinding through SKU rationalization and franchise consolidation.

Inventory was down 2% year-over-year to just over $1 billion, and the company repaid approximately $200 million of revolver borrowings, ending the quarter with no amounts outstanding under its $1.1 billion revolving credit facility.

The Fiscal 2025 Restructuring Plan has incurred $224 million of a total expected $255 million in charges, delivering approximately $35 million in savings in FY25 and on track for an additional $55 million in FY26.

Management stated it believes the December quarter marks the bottom of the North America reset and that the most disruptive phase of the turnaround is now behind the company, with the fall wholesale order book no longer showing significant declines.

CFO Dave Bergman is departing after 21 years at Under Armour and 9 years as CFO, with incoming CFO Reza set to take over, while several other leadership changes were announced including a new Chief Merchandising Officer, President of the Americas, and Chief Marketing Officer.
Total Q3 enrollments grew 1.8% to 244,500 and total revenue rose 2.7% to $629.9 million.

Career Learning (middle and high school) revenue grew nearly 16% to $259.5 million on enrollment growth of 11.6%, while General Education revenue fell 3.6% to $357.5 million on a 5% enrollment decline.
Total revenue per enrollment was $2,485, up 2.9% from $2,415, with full-year revenue per enrollment expected to be up roughly 2%.
Gross margin fell 380 basis points to 36.8%, with full-year gross margin guided to 37%–37.4%, pressured by platform rollout investments expected to moderate in FY2027.
Adjusted operating income was $140.4 million (down 1%), adjusted EBITDA was $171.3 million (up 1.8%), and adjusted EPS was $2.30 (down $0.03 year-over-year).
SG&A declined 13.5% to $102.5 million, with full-year SG&A guided to be down 6%–8% versus last year.
Free cash flow surged to $202.4 million from $37.3 million a year ago, and the company ended the quarter with $856 million in cash and marketable securities.

Full-year FY2026 guidance was narrowed to revenue of $2.490B–$2.520B and adjusted operating income of $490M–$500M, with Q4 revenue implied to be below the prior year due to marginally higher attrition and tougher funding true-up comparisons.

Management acknowledged marginally higher attrition since last quarter and noted enrollment windows were closed earlier this year as the company prioritized backfilling over growth, estimating thousands of potential enrollments were left on the table.

CEO described the new business development pipeline as 'as strong or stronger' than at any point in his 5-year tenure, and noted Pennsylvania's virtual funding cut could create opportunities for stronger players like Stride.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q3 2025 was $376 million compared to $347 million in the prior year period, with margin increasing 100 basis points year-over-year to 12.2%.
Same-store net revenue for Q3 increased 6.0% year-over-year, driven primarily by rate growth as net revenue per adjusted admission was up 5.6%.
The company reduced leverage to 6.7x at quarter end, down from 7.4x at year-end 2024.
CHS refinanced $1.743 billion of 2027 Senior Secured Notes through an offering of $1.79 billion of 9.75% Senior Secured Notes due 2034, pushing the nearest significant maturity to 2029.
Full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was tightened to $1.50 billion to $1.55 billion.
Q3 results included a $28 million gain from the settlement of prior litigation recognized as nonpatient revenue.
Same-store inpatient admissions increased 1.3% year-over-year, while same-store surgeries declined 2.2% and ED visits were down 1.3%.
Year-to-date adjusted cash flows from operations were $403 million when excluding $126 million in cash taxes paid on divestiture gains.
The company expects the divestiture of its outreach lab asset to close in Q4 2025 with proceeds of approximately $195 million.
At September 30, 2025, CHS had approximately 160 more employee physicians and advanced practice providers in clinics than in the prior year.
Consolidated net revenue for Q4 2025 was approximately $748 million, roughly flat compared to $750 million in Q4 2024.
Adjusted EBITDA for Q4 2025 reached a record $142 million with a record adjusted EBITDA margin of 19%, and adjusted net income was $88 million or $3.24 per diluted share.
Heavy commercial same-branch sales growth was 38% during Q4 2025, contributing approximately 40 basis points to gross margin improvement.
The company estimated weather impacts of approximately $20 million to first quarter 2026 revenue in January and February alone, which cannot be recovered in March.
IBP completed 11 acquisitions in 2025 representing over $64 million in annual revenue and expects to acquire at least $100 million of annual revenue in 2026.
The company generated $371 million in cash flow from operations for the 12 months ended December 31, 2025, a 9% year-over-year increase.
IBP closed a $500 million private offering of 5.625% senior notes due 2034 and expanded its revolving credit facility to $375 million, resulting in nearly $900 million in available liquidity.
The Board authorized a new $500 million stock buyback program through March 1, 2027, and declared a $1.80 per share annual variable dividend, a nearly 6% increase over the prior year.

Residential same-branch sales in the Installation segment declined 9% in Q4 2025, while full-year same-branch residential Installation segment sales were down 4%, with both single-family and multifamily decreasing.

Adjusted return on invested capital for 2025 was 24%, in line with returns achieved over the previous three years, and net debt to trailing 12-month adjusted EBITDA leverage was 1.1x versus a stated target of 2x.
AST SpaceMobile reported full year 2025 revenue of $70.9 million, achieving the top end of its guidance range of $50 million to $75 million.
The company expects full year 2026 revenue in the range of $150 million to $200 million, representing at least a doubling of 2025 revenue.
AST SpaceMobile sees the opportunity in 2027 approaching $1 billion in annual revenue, subject to achievement of commercial and government service objectives.

On a pro forma basis as of December 31, 2025, the company had approximately $3.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, restricted cash, and available ATM liquidity, which it says fully funds a constellation of over 100 satellites.
The company has signed over $1.2 billion in total contracted revenue commitments from commercial partners, though this represents a minority contribution to any individual year's revenue.

Capital expenditures for Q4 2025 were approximately $407 million, and Q1 2026 CapEx is expected in the range of $350 million to $425 million, primarily driven by launch payments and satellite materials.
The company remains on track to deploy 45 to 60 satellites into low Earth orbit by year-end 2026, with current expectations closer to 60 satellites ready to ship and 45 in orbit.
The average capital cost per satellite, including direct materials and launch costs, for over 90 Block 2 BlueBird satellites is estimated at $21 million to $23 million.
The company received a $175 million prepayment from stc Group as part of a 10-year commercial agreement covering Saudi Arabia and other markets in the Middle East and Africa.
Management indicated that long-term EBITDA margins could reach 90% or higher due to the fixed-cost nature of the business and its wholesale revenue-share go-to-market model with MNO partners.
Q1 2026 net revenue increased 21% year-over-year, with wholesale revenue up 31.5% (mass merchants +20%, grocery sales more than doubled) and direct-to-consumer revenue up 7%.
Adjusted EBITDA grew more than eightfold from under $1 million to over $7 million, representing 570 basis points of margin expansion year-over-year.
Q1 gross margin was 33%, down 305 bps year-over-year, impacted by ~210 bps from a one-time noncash coffee extract write-down and ~100 bps from onboarding a new DTC fulfillment provider.
Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to at least 8% revenue growth (~$430 million) and at least 35% adjusted EBITDA growth (~$29 million), up from prior guidance of at least 30% EBITDA growth.

Q2 2026 revenue is expected to grow at least 10% year-over-year (versus 21% in Q1) due to a few million dollars of shipment timing that benefited Q1, with Q2 adjusted EBITDA guided to at least $5 million.
Per Nielsen, Black Rifle Coffee grew 34.6% in the quarter—more than 2.5x the category—lifting bagged coffee dollar share 55 bps to 3.3% and pod share 45 bps to 2.2%.

Distribution expanded ~7 points of ACV year-over-year, with the average grocer now carrying nearly two more Black Rifle items than a year ago (averaging ~5.5 items, with some grocery customers carrying 13-14).
Of the 21% Q1 revenue growth, approximately 6% came from pricing with the vast majority driven by unit volume growth, and pricing is expected to fade in the back half.

The company ended the quarter with $39 million of debt (~1x net debt/TTM adjusted EBITDA), more than $52 million in total liquidity, and generated $6 million of free cash flow versus a $5 million use a year ago.

Green coffee requirements for 2026 are substantially locked, gross margin is guided to 34-36% (vs. 34.6% in 2025), and management reaffirmed a long-term 40% gross margin target not reliant on incremental pricing.
Q1 2026 revenue grew approximately 226% year-over-year to $71 million, with gross margins expanding to approximately 64% from 14% in the prior year period.

The company posted a net loss of $253.1 million and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $250.5 million for the quarter, driven primarily by unrealized mark-to-market adjustments on digital assets at Hut 8 and through the consolidation of American Bitcoin.

Hut 8 commercialized Phase 1 of its Beacon Point 1 gigawatt campus with a 15-year triple net lease for 352 MW of IT capacity (500 MW utility) to a AA- or higher investment-grade counterparty, generating $9.8 billion of expected base term contract value (with a 3% annual escalator) and up to over $25 billion including three 5-year renewal options.

Beacon Point's IT capacity was redesigned with NVIDIA as technology partner from 224 MW to 352 MW within the same land/utility footprint, increasing base term contract value by $3.6 billion from $6.2 billion to $9.8 billion.

After quarter-end, Hut 8 closed $3.25 billion of 16.5-year fully amortizing investment-grade (BBB-) senior secured notes for River Bend at a 6.192% coupon and approximately 95% loan-to-cost, recycling $184 million of previously deployed equity back to the company.

Combined contracted portfolio (River Bend + Beacon Point) is expected to generate approximately $16.8 billion of NOI over the 15-year initial lease terms and approximately $1.1 billion of annual NOI, with revenue flowing through to NOI at above 99.9% under the triple net structure.

Hut 8 refinanced its $200 million Coinbase Bitcoin-backed credit facility with a new 364-day FalconX note at a 7% coupon (down from 9%, a 200 bps improvement), unencumbering approximately 3,300 Bitcoin worth $260 million as of May 1 and bringing total unencumbered Bitcoin to approximately 5,600.

Compute segment revenue more than tripled to approximately $66 million from $16.1 million, with segment margins expanding to approximately 67% from 16%, as Bitcoin mined grew from 135 to 817 year-over-year despite average revenue per Bitcoin falling from $91,512 to $76,077.

The company exited Q1 with approximately $1.3 billion of parent-level cash and Bitcoin, with the Coatue convertible note (its only material parent recourse debt) deeply in the money and subject to mandatory redemption as soon as late June.

Management targets Q2 2027 for initial data hall delivery at River Bend, guided Beacon Point CapEx at $9-11 million per megawatt (consistent with River Bend), retains an 8.4 GW development pipeline, and disclosed that the tenant holds a ROFO on the remaining Beacon Point capacity, with 700 MW available in Q1 and another 300 MW in the following 24 months.
Q1 2026 revenue reached a record $403.9 million, up 75.8% year-over-year, with adjusted EBITDA increasing 29.7% to $194.9 million and adjusted EPS rising 91% to $1.30 from $0.68.

Energy Storage segment revenue grew 153.1% year-over-year with gross margin expanding to 59.1%, driven by favorable PJM merchant pricing and new capacity, though full-year 2026 storage gross margin is expected to moderate to 35%-40%.

Product segment revenue surged 458.4% to $177.4 million, including $105 million from the top two projects, representing approximately 60% of the segment's expected annual revenue, gross profit and EBITDA recognized in Q1.
The company maintained (rather than raised) its 2026 guidance of $1.11-$1.16 billion in revenue (14.6% YoY growth at midpoint) and adjusted EBITDA of $615-$645 million (8.2% growth at midpoint).

Ormat completed a $1 billion upsized convertible note offering, reducing its cost of debt to 3.9%, and used proceeds partly to repurchase shares at $108, incurring a $33.7 million one-time induced conversion expense.
Net debt stood at approximately $2.6 billion or 4.2x net debt to EBITDA, with cash and restricted cash of $763 million as of March 31, 2026 versus $281 million at year-end 2025.

Electricity segment revenue grew only ~1% to $181.6 million with gross margin declining to 30.8%, as high ambient temperatures in Nevada reduced revenue by approximately $4.8 million and Puna had lower energy rates.

The company signed PPAs for approximately 200 megawatts including agreements with Google and Switch, plus two blend-and-extend contracts; the CD4 Mammoth blend-and-extend extends the PPA five years to 2037 with pricing approximately 27% higher.
Management expects to collect approximately $90 million in 2026 from ITC tax equity transactions and PTC transfers, resulting in a negative tax rate of 15% to 20% for the year.

Ormat reaffirmed its 2.6-2.8 GW portfolio target by end of 2028, with 216 MW under construction in electricity and ~1.5 GWh of storage projects in development, while EGS pilots with SLB and Sage are expected to produce 2-4 MW each starting in 2027.
Total revenue for Q3 2025 was $54.5 million, with U.S. net sales of NERLYNX at $51.8 million compared to $48.8 million in Q3 2024.
Net income for Q3 2025 was $8.8 million ($0.18 per basic share), up from $5.9 million ($0.12 per share) in Q2 2025.
Puma raised full year 2025 NERLYNX net product revenue guidance to $198 million to $200 million, higher than prior guidance.
Full year 2025 net income is expected to be in the range of $27 million to $29 million.
The ALISCA-Breast1 trial has 98 patients enrolled with 14 in screening, enrolling ahead of expectations, with formal interim analysis anticipated in the first half of 2026.
Total outstanding principal debt decreased to approximately $33 million after a $11.1 million quarterly payment, with debt expected to be fully repaid by mid-2026.
Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities were approximately $94 million at September 30, 2025, compared to $101 million at year-end 2024.
Gross to net adjustment increased to 25.9% in Q3 2025 from 20.8% in Q2 2025, driven by higher Medicare rebates from the Inflation Reduction Act and higher Medicaid share.
According to current projections, 2025 will mark the first year-over-year demand increase for NERLYNX in the United States since 2018.
Q4 2025 guidance includes NERLYNX product revenue net of $54 million to $56 million, royalty revenue of $13 million to $14 million, and net income of $9 million to $11 million.
Q1 2026 originations reached $533 million, up 47% year-over-year from $363 million and 18% above the $451 million in Q1 2025, with March alone contributing $250 million.
Diluted EPS rose 22% to $0.24 from $0.19 a year earlier, while net income and pretax earnings each grew 18% to $5.5 million and $8 million respectively.
Revenues increased 5% to $112.3 million, driven by interest income of $108.7 million (up 6.7%), though the prior year included a $3.5 million fair value mark that was absent this quarter.
The fair value portfolio grew 11% year-over-year to $3.8 billion, yielding 11.3% net of losses.
Assets under management expanded to $3.942 billion, up 4.5% sequentially and 9% year-over-year.
Annualized net charge-offs rose to 8.57% of the average portfolio, up from 7.54% in Q1 2025, signaling worsening credit losses despite lower delinquencies.
Delinquencies over 30 days improved to 11.58% from 12.35% a year earlier, and recoveries increased to around 32% as weaker 2022-2023 vintages run off.
The company added 2,335 new and reactivated dealers to reach 10,544 active dealers (up 28% sequentially) and grew sales reps 29% to 124 from 96.
Monthly applications averaged 334,000, up 31% sequentially, while the capture rate improved 28% to 7.65% from 5.98%.
Core operating expenses fell 2% to $44.2 million, dropping to 4.6% of the managed portfolio from 5.1%, demonstrating portfolio growth without cost increases.
Kinetik reported Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $243 million, distributable cash flow of $158 million, and free cash flow of $51 million.
Full-year 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance was revised downward to $965 million to $1.005 billion, with a midpoint of $985 million.
The Midstream Logistics segment generated adjusted EBITDA of $151 million in Q3, down 13% year-over-year.
The delay in bringing Kings Landing fully online versus the original July 1 assumption reduced full-year earnings by approximately $20 million.
Waha natural gas pricing has declined by over 50% since the company's February assumptions.
In October, approximately 20% of volumes were curtailed on certain days, with roughly half from oil-focused producers.
The company received over $500 million in cash proceeds from the EPIC Crude sale and used proceeds to pay down debt, reducing leverage by approximately one-quarter of a turn.
Kinetik executed a 5-year European LNG pricing agreement with INEOS at Port Arthur LNG representing approximately 0.5 million tons per annum beginning in early 2027.
The Delaware Basin rig count has declined by nearly 20% since the beginning of the year.
The company has returned nearly $1.8 billion to shareholders since the merger in February 2022 and currently offers a total shareholder yield of nearly 11%.
Q4 2025 revenue was $113.3 million, up 66% year-over-year, with earnings per share tripling from $0.48 to $1.53.
Full year 2025 revenue reached $326.7 million, up 61% year-over-year, with non-GAAP EPS more than tripling from $0.93 to $3.20.
Q4 gross margins reached 61.2%, representing a 240 basis point improvement year-over-year and achieving the company's goal of exiting 2025 above 60%.
Book-to-bill was over 1.5 at the end of Q4, indicating strong demand visibility for 2026.

Communications, Enterprise, Data Center (CED) segment grew 160% year-over-year in Q4, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of over 100% year-over-year growth and now comprising 53% of total revenue.
Customers increased their 2026 forecast for oscillators used in 1.6T optical modules by 50%, in addition to a prior increase reported in November.

SiTime announced the acquisition of Renesas' timing business for $1.5 billion in cash and approximately 4.13 million newly issued SiTime shares, expected to add $300 million in revenue with approximately 70% gross margins in the 12 months after close.

The company plans to finance the acquisition using cash on hand and approximately $900 million of committed debt financing from Wells Fargo, with a path to reducing leverage to under 2x within 24 months of closing.
Q1 2026 guidance projects revenue of $101-$104 million (up approximately 70% year-over-year), gross margin of approximately 62%, and non-GAAP EPS of $1.10-$1.17.
Cash flow from operations was $87.2 million for fiscal 2025, a significant improvement from $23.2 million in 2024, with the company ending Q4 with $808 million in cash and short-term investments.
Q1 FY2026 revenue increased 1% to $52.7 million from $52.2 million in Q1 FY2025, in line with expectations.
Recurring revenues grew 8% year-over-year, with SaaS revenue up 24%, transaction-based revenue up 12%, and payments revenue up 8%, marking the fourth consecutive quarter of 20%-plus SaaS growth.
Annual recurring revenues increased 8% to $169.6 million in Q1 FY2026 from $156.4 million in Q1 FY2025, with 80% of quarterly revenues from recurring sources.

Adjusted EBITDA declined to $13.6 million (25.8% margin) in Q1 FY2026 from $14.6 million (27.9% margin) in Q1 FY2025, driven by market investments, higher hosting costs, and $2.6 million lower professional services revenues.

The company acquired a driver and motor vehicle insurance verification software provider effective January 1 for $60 million in cash at approximately 15x EBITDA, with the target growing above 20% and carrying an EBITDA margin above 50%.
As of December 31, the company had $37 million of cash and no debt, with a $400 million revolving credit facility available at a 5x leverage constraint.
FY2026 guidance was set at revenues of $223 million to $234 million, adjusted EBITDA of $61 million to $66.5 million, and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.08 to $1.16.

Professional services revenue outlook for FY2026 was revised down from an expected $33 million to $31 million, compared to $40 million in FY2025, reflecting project revenue recognition cadence in utilities and transportation markets.
Management confirmed the company repurchased a significant number of shares during the quarter, with details to be disclosed in the upcoming 10-Q filing.
Organic recurring revenue growth is expected at 8% to 10% for FY2026, with SaaS growth expected to exceed 30% for the rest of the fiscal year including the acquisition contribution.

Carrier's data center business grew to around $1 billion in 2025, with Q4 CSA data center orders up more than 4x year-over-year, and the company is guiding data center revenue to approximately $1.5 billion in 2026 (up about 50%).
The company distributed $3.7 billion to shareholders through buybacks and dividends in 2025 and intends to repurchase about $1.5 billion in shares in 2026.
Full year 2025 free cash flow was approximately $2.1 billion, and 2026 free cash flow is expected to be approximately $2 billion.

Adjusted EPS is expected to be approximately $2.80 in 2026, up high single digits versus 2025, with Q1 2026 adjusted EPS expected to be about $0.50 including a benefit from an approximately 0% effective tax rate due to a discrete tax item.

Cost actions executed in 2025, including a reduction of 3,000 heads, are expected to deliver over $100 million of savings in 2026, with total productivity including cost actions expected to be close to $400 million.

CSA Residential sales were down nearly 40% in Q4 2025 with volume down over 40%, and the company expects CSA Resi to be down over 20% in Q1 2026, with full year sales down high single digits including low single-digit price realization.
The company estimates industry residential units will be down 10% to 15% in 2026, with field inventories down roughly 30% year-over-year to 2018-level lows at year-end.
Total company Q4 2025 orders were up over 16%, with CSA Commercial orders up 80% and applied orders within CSA Commercial more than tripling year-over-year.

For 2026, the company expects approximately $22 billion in reported sales with flat to low mid-single-digit organic growth and adjusted operating profit of about $3.4 billion, with volume/mix a headwind of about $100 million offset by ~$400 million in productivity.

The company faces approximately $60 million in net commodity headwinds (copper, steel, aluminum) for 2026 and is just over 50% blocked for the full year, while also noting a roughly $350 million revenue headwind from the Riello exit.
Q1 2026 total sales were $317 million, down 1.3% year-over-year, but increased 3.8% as reported (2.1% in constant currency) excluding the GI divestiture impact.
Adjusted net income was $27.1 million (down 8.5% YoY) and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.89 (down 6.3% YoY), impacted by the GI business exit.
CONMED raised its 2026 organic growth guidance to 5.0%-6.5% (from 4.5%-6.0%) and reported revenue guidance to $1.35B-$1.375B, while maintaining adjusted EPS guidance of $4.30-$4.45.
The company expects debt refinancing in Q2 to be done with bank debt rather than convertible notes due to historic low med tech multiples, adding at least $0.10 of headwind to full-year adjusted EPS.

2026 GI product line revenue guidance was lowered to $14.5M-$17.5M (from $21M-$25M), roughly $7M lower at the midpoint, due to faster-than-expected divestitures to Gore, Micro-Tech, and an undisclosed strategic acquirer.
Q1 adjusted gross margin expanded 100 bps YoY to 57.4%, at the top of the 50-100 bps full-year improvement guidance range.
Orthopedics grew 4.5% in constant currency in Q1, marking the third consecutive quarter of at least mid-single-digit growth, while general surgery declined 7.4% constant currency but was flat ex-GI.

AirSeal added more capital units in Q1 than the market-leading robotic systems, with U.S. AirSeal unit placements up over 50% versus Q1 2025, and the platform's installed base exceeds 10,000 systems globally with only 6%-7% U.S. laparoscopic penetration.

Buffalo Filter smoke evacuation now has 20 U.S. states with smoke-free OR laws covering ~51% of the population, with 13 additional states having bills pending (Maryland and Massachusetts most likely to pass next).

The company repurchased ~858,000 shares for $37.4 million in Q1, ended with a 3.1x leverage ratio (targeting ~3x), and reaffirmed full-year operating cash flow guidance of $145M-$155M and free cash flow of ~$125M.
IAM customers are generating over $350 million in ARR after just 18 months, representing 10.8% of total company ARR, up from 2.3% at the end of fiscal 2025.

Q4 billings exceeded $1 billion for the first time in DocuSign's history, growing 10% year-over-year, with approximately half the outperformance versus guidance driven by timing and the remainder from FX and bookings.

Fiscal 2026 was the first year with non-GAAP operating margins exceeding 30% and free cash flow surpassing $1 billion (33% margin), with Q4 free cash flow of $350 million representing 25% year-over-year growth.

The company expanded its share repurchase program by $2 billion to a total remaining authorization of $2.6 billion, and repurchased $869 million in stock in fiscal 2026, representing 82% of annual free cash flow.
DocuSign expects IAM to represent approximately 18% of total ARR by the end of fiscal 2027, driving IAM to well over $600 million in ARR.

ARR guidance for fiscal 2027 anticipates accelerating growth to 8.25%-8.75% year-over-year, reaching $3.551 billion at the midpoint, with growth driven by gross new bookings from IAM customers and gross retention improvements.
Total partner-contributed bookings grew by over 30% year-over-year in Q4, reflecting an improved contribution from the partner channel to the direct business.

The number of private consented agreements ingested into DocuSign Navigator expanded to over 200 million, up from 150 million in December, and the company has optimized AI processing costs by upwards of 50x compared to running direct prompts on LLMs.
International revenue surpassed 30% of total revenue in Q4 and grew 15% year-over-year, while customers spending over $300,000 annually increased 7% year-over-year to 1,205.

Fiscal 2027 non-GAAP operating margin is guided at 30.0%-30.5%, with the company reinvesting go-to-market efficiencies into increased R&D investment in enterprise, AI, legal tech, U.S. federal, and security.
Atlas generated $40.2 million of adjusted EBITDA on $260 million of revenue in Q3 2025, delivering a 15% adjusted EBITDA margin.
Q3 proppant volumes were 5.25 million tons, with Q4 expected to decline to approximately 4.8 million tons, which management forecasts to be the low point during the cycle.
OpEx per ton including royalties rose to $13.52, driven primarily by dredge feed and wet shed challenges at the Kermit facility.
The company has temporarily suspended its dividend, citing insufficient profitability to cover the dividend and capital requirements for power market opportunities.
Atlas is targeting more than 400 megawatts deployed across its power business by early 2027, with the majority under long-term contracts.
The company placed an order for more than 240 megawatts of new power generation assets with a blue-chip equipment provider.
Atlas's power opportunity pipeline is now approaching 2 gigawatts in potential projects.
The company launched a company-wide efficiency initiative with an initial target of $20 million in annual cost savings, with full impact expected by mid-2026.
Management estimates Atlas's Permian market share has grown during the downcycle to approximately 35%, with early RFP signals suggesting further growth next year.
The company expects the Dune Express to exceed 10 million tons in 2026, representing a major ramp from 2025 levels.
Q3 2025 revenue grew nearly 12% year-over-year to $74.7 million, with product revenue up 17% to $43.1 million and service revenue up 6% to $31.6 million.
Revenue from the Americas increased 25% on a trailing 12-month basis, driven primarily by investment in AI infrastructure.
EBITDA margins expanded year-over-year from 26.7% to 29.3%, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded from 22.6% to 24.7%.
Non-GAAP EPS was $0.23 per diluted share, reflecting 7.4% growth from the year-ago period.
Cash and investments totaled $371 million at the end of the quarter, with $22.8 million generated in cash flow from operations.
Security-led revenue exceeded the company's long-term target of 65% of total revenue in Q3.
